html:
The Battle of Sisak was fought on 22 June 1593 at the fortress of Sisak in central Croatia, where Habsburg and Croatian troops destroyed an Ottoman army under Hasan Pasha Predojević of Bosnia.

The Ottomans had pushed deep into Croatia through the 1500s, and the country was reduced to a small remnant around Zagreb. At Sisak, where the Kupa meets the Sava, the Ottomans were caught crossing the river, and thousands drowned or were killed, including their commander. The victory set off the Long Turkish War between the Habsburgs and the Ottomans, and it marked the end of Ottoman expansion in Croatia. It is still celebrated as a national turning point.
